title: The Danger of Pipe Backfall in Waste Lines
description: A common mistake in waste pipe installation is failing to maintain a consistent downward slope, leading to backfall or flat sections. When a horizontal waste pipe lacks proper pitch or slants backward, wastewater stops moving efficiently, allowing heavy solids to settle while liquids slowly flow over them. Over time, this leads to chronic blockages, foul odors, and pipe corrosion. Always verify pipe pitch using a reliable spirit level before permanently securing pipe hangers. Correct grading ensures proper scouring velocity, keeping the waste line clean and free-flowing.
caption:
The Danger of Pipe Backfall in Waste Lines

A common mistake in waste pipe installation is failing to maintain a consistent downward slope, leading to backfall or flat sections. When a horizontal waste pipe lacks proper pitch or slants backward, wastewater stops moving efficiently, allowing heavy solids to settle while liquids slowly flow over them. Over time, this leads to chronic blockages, foul odors, and pipe corrosion. Always verify pipe pitch using a reliable spirit level before permanently securing pipe hangers. Correct grading ensures proper scouring velocity, keeping the waste line clean and free-flowing.
